name: Abr Baran IDC Arak
notes: Operator page identifies Abr Baran as a datacenter in Arak, Markazi province, offering dedicated/cloud servers, cloud hosting, colocation, GPU servers, and 24-hour technical support; supporting company article says its first and second halls are in Arak.

name: Markazi Province Gas Company data center
notes: IRIB reported a new data center for the Markazi Province Gas Company opened in Markazi province to improve information security and communications infrastructure.

name: Parsdev Rasht data center
notes: Parsdev states it provides hosting and datacenter services and has physical branches in Rasht and Tehran; Data Center Map lists Parsdev Rasht on Prophethood Street, Rasht, Guilan. Operator page is primary for the company, while facility address detail is third-party.

name: Mihan Web Host data centers
developer: Net Mihan Communications / Mihan Web Host
notes: Mihan Web Host says it launched its first dedicated datacenter in summer 1394 and currently hosts five data centers with 200 sq m space and 2000-server capacity; the provider is based in Rasht, Guilan, though the public page describes a multi-location network including Rasht, Tehran, Isfahan, and Tabriz.

name: IranCell Sari / Mazandaran provincial data center initiative
notes: Iranian parliament news agency reported that launching an Irancell datacenter in the provincial capital, Sari, and using fiber capacity were discussed and coordination was to be arranged; no later completion evidence found in this pass.

name: Islamic Azad University Sari data center
notes: ANA reported the developed Sari Islamic Azad University data center opened with 200 sq m area, more than 6.5 billion rial investment, nominal 40 physical servers supporting over 600 virtual servers, and over 50,000 GB storage.

name: MCI Shahid Qazi Tabatabai / Tabriz regional data center
developer: Mobile Telecommunication Company of Iran (Hamrah-e Aval / MCI)
notes: Mehr and MCI reported opening of the largest west/northwest Iran data center in Tabriz, with 3,000 sq m technical/administrative area over three floors and 350 billion toman investment, supporting cloud, MCI network resilience, traffic distribution, IX connectivity, and content services.

name: ArvanCloud Shahriar Tabriz data center
notes: Zoomit advertorial reported ArvanCloud opened the Shahriar data center in Tabriz as its first outside Tehran/center, Tier 3, initially 16 racks with another 16 planned, hosting cloud servers and later object storage POP; Arvan's network page lists Tabriz presence.

name: Iranfanni IDC Tabriz
notes: Data Center Map archived listing describes Iranfanni IDC at Tabriz Baghmishe with claimed establishment in 2003 and multiple 1G Internet ports, but marks the listing no longer active; status could be closed or replaced.

name: Maku Free Zone national datacenter hub
developer: Private-sector partner with West Azerbaijan ICT authorities / Maku Free Zone
notes: Iran ICT ministry reported West Azerbaijan's ICT director said a fourth national datacenter hub would be created in Maku Free Zone with private-sector participation and 3,000 racks; article also named Alborz, Fars, and Razavi Khorasan as other hubs.

name: West Azerbaijan Governorate data center
notes: Donya-e-Eqtesad reported the West Azerbaijan Governorate data center opened in Urmia to aggregate communications for governorate buildings and subordinate county offices, including fiber, state network, monitoring, web hosting, automation, and virtualization.

name: Kermanshah advanced western Iran data center proposal
developer: Kermanshah provincial government / Telecommunications Company of Iran stakeholders
notes: Mehr reported Kermanshah governor requested creation of a large advanced datacenter in Kermanshah, arguing the province is the best point for western Iran processing and storage due to geography and west-province connectivity; treated as planned/proposed because no construction start was found.

name: Kermanshah western Iran educational data center
developer: Kermanshah education authorities / smart high school project
notes: Mehr reported the first educational data center in western Iran opened in Kermanshah province with domestic high-speed fiber-connected servers and 150 TB storage capacity, supporting virtual classes and online exams.

name: ArvanCloud Gheysar Ahvaz data center
notes: Zoomit and Digiato reported ArvanCloud opened the Gheysar data center in Ahvaz, its fifth Iranian data center and third in-country compute region after Tehran and Tabriz, enabling multi-region architecture and lower latency for southern/western users.

name: Khuzestan provincial data center
notes: Mehr reported the country's first provincial data center opened in Khuzestan with about 40 billion rial investment by the Iran Information Technology Organization to support online/electronic services and balanced provincial ICT development.

name: MCI large south Iran data center in Shiraz
developer: Mobile Telecommunication Company of Iran (Hamrah-e Aval / MCI)
notes: Zoomit reported MCI began construction of a large south-Iran data center in Shiraz with 300-rack capacity, five times larger than the existing Shiraz data center, 1,000 billion toman investment, and an 18-month completion target. Current completion status was not confirmed in this pass.

name: Dourbord / Shiraz Electronic Tower data center
developer: Dourbord Communications Engineering; Shiraz Electronic Tower / MAGFA
notes: ILNA and Fars report the Shiraz Electronic Tower datacenter opened as the first Ministry-licensed southern Iran data center, ANSI/TIA-942:2017 aligned, implemented by Dourbord with more than 400 billion rial investment; Fars notes phase two was also being prepared.

name: Arvina Kerman data center
developer: Arvina; Tose'e Pardaz Farzan; NoAyin Technology Group
notes: Arvina says its Kerman data center began activity in 1403 with joint investment by Tose'e Pardaz Farzan and NoAyin Technology Group, offering cloud services, dedicated servers, colocation/shared space, 24/7 monitoring, UPS backup, and 2 x 10 Gbps fiber uplinks.

name: Kerman provincial data center / Cloud Iran node
notes: Iran ICT ministry said provincial data centers were the second layer of the National Information Network and that data centers in Fars, Kerman, Golestan, and Razavi Khorasan were being prepared/completed; later Cloud Iran reporting described provincial datacenter infrastructure being transferred for cloud development in multiple cities. Specific current Kerman operator status remains limited.

name: Tus Data Center Mashhad
notes: Tus Data Center operator page states it is a Mashhad-based data center offering colocation and dedicated server rental, with UPS/generator power, 99.99% uptime claim, direct connection to national backbone infrastructure, BGP/IP announcement, and institutional customers in Mashhad/Razavi Khorasan.

name: Asiatech Mashhad data center / IDC presence
notes: CITNA reported Asiatech expanded IDC services geographically to Tabriz, Shiraz, and Mashhad with more than 2.4 PB active content storage and over 650 Gbps domestic content traffic; Asiatechin currently advertises colocation in Mashhad alongside Tabriz, Qom, and Hamedan.
